Read CAMELS-PE Soil Classes

Source: R/soil.R
read_soil_classes.Rd

Reads the areal percentages of the soil suborders, great groups and horizon texture classes of the CAMELS-PE catchments, derived from the Digital Soil Map DSOLMap (USDA Soil Taxonomy). The available levels are:

read_soil_classes(
  level = NULL,
  gauge_id = NULL,
  format = c("long", "wide"),
  path = get_camels_path()
)

Arguments

level

Character vector or NULL. One or more of "suborder", "great_group", "texture_h1", "texture_h2" and "texture_h3". If NULL, all levels are returned. With format = "wide", a single level must be given.

gauge_id

Character vector or NULL. Optional gauge identifiers used to filter the data. If NULL, all catchments are returned.

format

Character string. "long" (default) returns the table as stored in the dataset, one row per catchment, level and class, with the class name, order and suborder from the legend. "wide" returns one row per catchment and one <class>_perc column per class.

path

Character string. Optional path to the CAMELS-PE root directory. If not provided, the path previously defined with set_camels_path() is used.

Value

A tibble with the soil class percentages of each catchment.

Details

  • "suborder": soil suborders (e.g. Ochrepts, Udults).

  • "great_group": soil great groups (e.g. cryochrepts, tropudults).

  • "texture_h1", "texture_h2", "texture_h3": USDA texture classes of the three horizons with which DSOLMap describes each soil unit, from the shallowest (h1) to the deepest (h3).

The percentages of the soil orders and the dominant order, suborder, great group and horizon textures are read with read_attributes("soil"). Use read_soil_legend() to see the hierarchy order > suborder > great group.

The data are read from 02_attributes/soil_classes.csv. All classes present in at least one catchment are listed, with 0 where absent, and the classes of each level sum to 100\

The suborders and great groups follow the DSOLMap legend, which uses names of the USDA Soil Taxonomy prior to 1999 (e.g. Ochrepts). DSOLMap does not give the depth of the horizons.

In long format, the columns are gauge_id, level, class, name, order, suborder and perc.

Examples

path <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  "sample_camels_pe",
  package = "RCamelsPE"
)

# Suborders of one catchment, in long format
sub <- read_soil_classes(
  level = "suborder",
  gauge_id = "PE_212900",
  path = path
)
sub[sub$perc > 0, ]
#> # A tibble: 11 × 7
#>    gauge_id  level    class     name      order       suborder  perc
#>    <chr>     <chr>    <chr>     <chr>     <chr>       <chr>    <dbl>
#>  1 PE_212900 suborder udalfs    Udalfs    Alfisols    NA        1.55
#>  2 PE_212900 suborder ustalfs   Ustalfs   Alfisols    NA        1.46
#>  3 PE_212900 suborder argids    Argids    Aridisols   NA        0.18
#>  4 PE_212900 suborder fluvents  Fluvents  Entisols    NA        8.82
#>  5 PE_212900 suborder orthents  Orthents  Entisols    NA        1.27
#>  6 PE_212900 suborder psamments Psamments Entisols    NA       20.1 
#>  7 PE_212900 suborder orthels   Orthels   Gelisols    NA        0.07
#>  8 PE_212900 suborder ochrepts  Ochrepts  Inceptisols NA       66.2 
#>  9 PE_212900 suborder orthox    Orthox    Oxisols     NA        0.02
#> 10 PE_212900 suborder ustox     Ustox     Oxisols     NA        0.02
#> 11 PE_212900 suborder udults    Udults    Ultisols    NA        0.29

# Texture of the shallowest horizon, one column per texture class
read_soil_classes(level = "texture_h1", format = "wide", path = path)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   gauge_id  sand_perc loamy_sand_perc sandy_loam_perc loam_perc silt_loam_perc
#>   <chr>         <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl>     <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 PE_212900         0               0           24.9       66.4              0
#> 2 PE_200907         0               0            5.47      29.2              0
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: silt_perc <dbl>, sandy_clay_loam_perc <dbl>,
#> #   clay_loam_perc <dbl>, silty_clay_loam_perc <dbl>, sandy_clay_perc <dbl>,
#> #   silty_clay_perc <dbl>, clay_perc <dbl>
